Every supplied statement is used exactly once inside one of the two chains. The chains share no intermediate individuals (note that Sara/Sarah and Julia/Julie are treated as distinct because the source statements spell them differently and never equate them). Consequently, both Janet and Harold are ancestors of Kevin, so Janet and Harold share at least one common descendant. No statement produces a path from Harold to Janet (or conversely), ruling out an ancestor-descendant relation between them, and the chains supply no common ancestor above the merge point at Kevin.
